claim: As of Skype version 7.0, H.264 was used for both group and one-on-one video chat
On 11 November 2014, Microsoft announced Lync would be replaced by Skype for Business in 2015
Skype's WiFi service was retired globally on 31 March 2017 to focus on core Skype features
Microsoft's stated reason for killing Skype WiFi was to better focus on core Skype features
Skype WiFi covered more than 2 million hotspots globally at 2017 shutdown
The Skype WiFi service became non-functional from 31 March 2017
Skype's third-party Extras program was closed on 11 September 2009 due to low usage
Skype version 7.0 (Skype classic) would no longer function after September 1, 2018
Skype 7.0/Classic would work until the cutoff date, after which users needed version 8.0
Skype 7.x Windows installer builds include 7.36.0.101/.150, 7.40.0.103/.104/.151, 7.41.0.101
Skype Translator discontinued for old clients on January 22, 2018
Beginning Feb 1, 2019 Microsoft forcibly updated all remaining Skype 7.x to Skype 8
Skype app versions 7.17-7.30 on Windows Desktop dropped from support Sept 4, 2017
Microsoft shut down third-party Desktop API access end of 2013, retained call recording/hardware compatibility after backlash
Skype 7.0 redesign introduced chat bubbles in soft blue, rounded avatars, better notifications
Skype 7 chat window shows shared images in-line instantly once downloaded
Skype 7 Windows increased spacing between contacts list and chat window
Skype 7 shows message previews for unread messages in contacts/chat list
Skype 7 redesign made it easier to chat alongside a video or voice call
Skype 7.0.0.102 added setting to hide/show big emoticons
Skype 7.0.0.102 renamed 'Standard view mode' to 'Showing a single window'
Skype 7.0.0.102 renamed 'Simple List' to 'Compact sidebar'
Skype 7.0.0.102 updated color scheme and compact interface mode
Skype 7.0.0.102 renamed compact-view chat setting to reference Split Window View
Skype 7.0.0.102 changed SMS field from 'Send SMS' button to 'Type an SMS here' placeholder
Skype 7.0.0.102 (5 Dec 2014) added friendlier touchscreen interface
Skype 7.0.0.102 added sending/receiving images while recipient/sender offline
Skype 7.0.0.102 added 'show all' option for multiple sent files
Skype Options > Notifications nav pane has Notification Settings, Alerts & Messages, Sounds
Skype Options > Notifications > Sounds lets users uncheck sound triggers for various events
'Not Available' status supported since Skype 4, removed in Skype 5
'SkypeMe!' presence indicator invited calls from strangers, hidden in Skype 4, removed in Skype 5
Skype 5+ display others' 'Not Available' status as 'Away'
Skype allows removing/editing messages within one hour after sending
Skype emoticon set includes about 254 emoticons, static or animated
Skype has hidden emoticons plus 241 flag emoticons and 63 other emoticons
Skype supports group text chat similar to IRC with up to 150 people
Skype group chats have Creator/Moderator and User roles; no UI button to promote to Admin
Promote to Admin via chat command '/setrole [SkypeName] Admin'
'/showmembers' command lists Users and Admins in group chat
Skype Name (distinct from display name) found via right-click > View Profile
Skype file transfers limited to 100MB per file (reported May 2016)
Skype raised file-sharing limit to 300MB for files/photos/videos
Read receipts not part of Skype 7.x; introduced Sept 2018 Insider Preview build
H.264 used for group/one-on-one video chat at SD, 720p, 1080p as of v7.0
Free conference calls/video/screen share limited to 25 people, increased to 50 on 5 April 2019
On April 28, 2014 Skype made group video calling free again, up to nine others, screen sharing included, desktop/Xbox One only
Group video calls became paid feature in early 2011, before Microsoft's ~$8B acquisition
Online Number (SkypeIn) let users receive calls from conventional phone subscribers dialing a local Skype number
Existing Skype Credit balance for outgoing calls can be used via Skype Dial Pad web app
Skype added native call recording Sept 4, 2018; plus-sign > Start recording; MP4 stored 30 days
Call recording available on every platform except Windows 10 at Sept 2018 launch
Call recording triggers banner notification to all participants; Microsoft recommended verbal consent notice
Before native recording, users relied on third-party apps like MP3 Skype Recorder
